pr_title: Shaders: Perform equivalent frustum test in `getPointShadow()` like in `getShadow()`.
pr_body:
Fixed #27916.

**Description**

This PR makes the shadow mask computed by `getPointShadow()` more consistent to `getShadow()` by performing a similar frustum test based on the near/far value of the shadow camera and the fragment's distance to the shadow's camera position.

issue_context.title: Shadowmaterial goes dark when pointlight.distance is set
issue_context.body:
### Description

Hello guys,

I might have found a bug related to pointlights and ShadowMaterials. Or maybe I am too dumb.

When I have a Plane with a ShadowMaterial which receives shadows it works when I add a PointLight with pointLight.distance = 0. 
However, when I change the distance to a non zero value, the whole Shadowplane goes dark except for the area that receives light. Why so? Shouldn't it be as transparent as before? 

I tried in the threejs editor aswell, with the same result.. It does feel very odd, so I had a feeling to open this issue

PS: sorry for not providing a fiddle, somehow I can't get the fiddle to work with shadowplanes at all...

### Reproduction steps

1. Add Ambient Light to scene
2. Add a big ground plane to the scene, rotate it by 90° and apply a ShadowMaterial to it
3. Add a PointLight to the scene (default value of pointLight.distance is 0 === infinity)
4. Place a cube above the ground plane to see a that the (until now) transparent shadowplane works
5. Change the pointLight.distance to a non-zero value ===> Whole Shadowplane goes dark


### Code

https://threejs.org/editor/

### Live example

https://threejs.org/editor/

### Screenshots

Before changing pointLight.distance ==> looks good, transparent shadowplane
![pointlightShadowBug1](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/69421749/7b74e009-de0b-4800-abe0-719cd9c928aa)

After changing pointLight.distance ==> Why is the rest of the Shadowplane black / shadowed now?
![pointLightShadowBug2](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/69421749/99dc8ecb-f086-46bd-830d-e52182133707)

Another example from my own code: 

1. with pointLight distance = 3: 
![image](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/69421749/8542d3b8-9586-4766-abee-37e9525d4d04)

2. with pointlight.distance = 0: 

![image](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/assets/69421749/89461ae6-d6bf-45fc-900f-9e0bda9a6142)

### Version

r151

### Device

Desktop

### Browser

Chrome

### OS

Windows
comments: The following exported application can be used to reproduce the issue. Just drag'n'drop it into the editor: [app.json](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/files/14599667/app.json) Initially, the point light has a distance of `5` which looks like so: If you increase it to `10`, you get:
Reconsidering the issue. I understand now that a transparent surface is expected when no light hits the surface.

Thank you! For a moment I was shocked ^^" 
Do you have a feeling where this issue is coming from and how I can workaround that? Maybe don't rely on ShadowMaterial or smth? 
I feel like for any other material the behaviour would have been expected, but not for ShadowMaterials? I have tried to find the shader code or smth itself but unfortunately couldn't find it.

`SpotLight` works as expected so let's consider this as a bug in `PointLight` (specifically `getPointShadow()`).

Maybe this can be fixed by implementing a similar frustum test in `getPointShadow()` like in `getShadow()` 🤔 .

review_comments: Wouldn't it be simpler to just check whether `dp >= 0.0 && dp <= 1.0`?
